changes: Clock is Compustat FYEAR t, a fiscal-year label; EARN(t+1) and the return event remain one year ahead. Original t window 1981–1999 is pooled with t=2000–2004; the separate 13,012-observation SFAS 95 accrual-decomposition sample is not the assigned Table 2 baseline population.

Expanded the accepted COMP.FUNDA extraction to FYEAR 1980–2005 to supply t−1/t/t+1 statements for t through 2004. Extended the existing CRSP.MSF, CRSP.MSIX and CRSP.MSEDELIST windows through 2006-12-31, size-cap input through 2005-12-31, prior-December rank years through 2004 and first-in-year rank years through 2005. Kept the four-month post-DATADATE holding start, 12 monthly returns, currency/link rules and accepted likelihood unchanged.

Rebuilt the historical and added years together from the named local source files. The pooled strict 1st/99th BKLG trim used cutoffs 0.007912 and 4.049303 on 29,698 complete pretrim rows; 592 observations were removed, leaving 29,106 firm-years. The added FY2000–FY2004 portion contributes 4,389 estimation observations; every year 2000–2004 is represented.

Used the existing FYEAR variable in the final handoff to count the active Stata e(sample) by original and added periods. The joint likelihood has the same estimation sample for both assigned equation rows; standalone EXT_SAMPLE records were produced by the native cell.
Moved the two assigned Table 2 outputs to work/artifacts so the report can reference fresh aggregate-only tables.
limitations: The paper describes iterative weighted nonlinear least squares and nonlinear GLS, but the observation weights and cross-equation error restriction are unspecified. This replay preserves the accepted independent-error conditional Gaussian maximum-likelihood implementation; it is a labeled best-effort estimator, not an exact recovery of the paper’s undisclosed weighting.

The local Compustat and CRSP files are the current local vintages recorded in launch.json, not the authors’ stated 2000 tapes. The published N=21,891 remains a comparison point, not a target used to tune construction.

The accepted local construction reconstructs annual target size deciles from historical CRSP price-times-shares and dated names. It uses calendar-year-end formation (with a constrained first-cap fallback) and compounds value-weighted, annually rebalanced MSIX returns; the paper describes a mean-return buy-and-hold size portfolio. Membership, formation timing and weighting therefore remain approximate.

Mixed-currency ratios use the accepted ratio-specific dated GBP-intermediary translation: daily FX for assets/backlog and EXRAT12M at statement month for IB. Same-currency ratios remain in native units; unsupported mixed ratios remain unavailable.

The pooled trim is recomputed across 1981–2004, so its original-period component (N=24,717) is not row-identical to the prior original-only fit (N=24,696). Reported coefficient comparisons use the same accepted estimator and table output, but different pooled sample cutoffs.

The accepted Compustat source audit found 2 duplicate GVKEY/FYEAR groups (2 extra rows) in its filtered FY1980–FY2005 extract. The accepted FINAL/FDATE/PDATE/DATADATE sort preference was retained; the aggregate build log does not date those two source groups. The final pooled table has 0 duplicate GVKEY/FYEAR keys, and the Stata handoff uniqueness assertion passed.

This assigned extension covers only the jointly estimated Table 2 forecasting and returns equations. Other paper analyses, including IBES forecast, SFAS 95 operating-cash-flow decomposition and control-variable branches, are outside the assigned scopes and receive no extended result here.
